name: SQLite and DuckDB analytical workflow
summary: A candidate local workflow that keeps SQLite as the transactional source and uses DuckDB for analytical processing over an explicitly refreshed derived snapshot.

features.name: Transactional source with analytical reader
features.description: The proposed boundary keeps SQLite responsible for transactional state and gives DuckDB a refreshed derived snapshot for analytical queries.

mathematical_views.question: Under what refresh and visibility conditions can an analytical reader consume a derived SQLite state without being mistaken for the transactional authority?
assumptions: SQLite remains the only write authority for the source state
The handoff exports a defined committed snapshot rather than sharing undocumented file state
DuckDB analytical results are interpreted relative to the snapshot version and refresh time

benefits: Separates transactional write concerns from analytical execution concerns
Allows each embedded engine to retain its documented workload focus
costs: Introduces snapshot refresh, freshness, and duplicate-storage coordination
The host process must budget resources for both engines

evidence.title: Appropriate Uses For SQLite
evidence.notes: Reviewed SQLite evidence for embedded/local deployment and concurrency boundaries.

evidence.title: Write-Ahead Logging
evidence.notes: Reviewed SQLite evidence for reader snapshots, writer concurrency, and checkpoint behavior.

evidence.title: Atomic Commit In SQLite
evidence.notes: Reviewed SQLite evidence for atomic commit, recovery, and filesystem assumptions.

evidence.title: Why DuckDB
evidence.notes: Reviewed DuckDB evidence for embedded operation and vectorized analytical execution.

inputs.role: analytical reader over a derived snapshot

constraints.description: SQLite remains the sole write authority; the DuckDB side must consume a defined exported or copied snapshot rather than assuming undocumented concurrent writes to SQLite storage.
Each analytical result must carry the source snapshot identity or refresh boundary so consumers can distinguish current transactional state from derived analytical state.
The host must provision enough process memory, I/O, and scheduling capacity for both embedded engines; the composition does not create an isolation boundary.

preserved_properties.description: SQLite's documented transaction and crash-recovery behavior remains the source-of-record durability contract under its filesystem and synchronization assumptions.
DuckDB retains its documented embedded, vectorized analytical execution role for queries against the derived snapshot.

conflicts.description: A refresh boundary can make DuckDB results stale relative to SQLite commits, so the workflow cannot promise read-after-write equivalence without an explicit synchronization protocol.
Running analytical work in the same host environment can compete with SQLite for CPU, memory, and I/O, especially for large scans.

validation_gaps.description: The reviewed evidence does not establish a supported SQLite-to-DuckDB snapshot connector or interchange path for the selected versions.
An end-to-end prototype is needed to test snapshot creation, refresh atomicity, freshness reporting, and behavior while SQLite readers and writers are active.
A workload benchmark is needed to measure refresh cost and host-resource interference across transactional writes and analytical scans.
